meta_title: Master of the Night — Vampire: The Eternal Struggle in your browser
meta_description: Play Vampire: The Eternal Struggle for free, in your browser: online tables for 1 to 5 players, a guided tutorial, AI opponents and a deck builder. Formerly VTES Mobile.
og_description: Vampire: The Eternal Struggle, in your browser. Free, nothing to install.
kicker: Vampire: The Eternal Struggle, in your browser
hero_lede: Richard Garfield's card game on a real five-player table, with the rules enforced for you — free, nothing to install, no account needed to start.
hero_hint: The first launch takes a moment while the cards load; after that the game stays cached. A PC or tablet screen is recommended.
table_aria: Diagram of a five-player table: prey and predator
table_caption: With five players, everyone bleeds the player on their left — their prey — and defends against the one on their right — their predator. The other two are neither: natural negotiating partners, whose interests do not always match yours. When your prey falls, their prey becomes yours.
what_title: What is Vampire: The Eternal Struggle?
what_sub: Born in 1994 as Jyhad, the other card game by Richard Garfield, the designer of Magic.
what_p1: You are a Methuselah, a vampire so ancient that you only act through others. Your pawns are younger vampires you awaken one by one, and your pool of blood is your life: when it reaches zero, you are out of the game.
what_p2: What makes VTES unique is the table. It is not a duel but a multiplayer game, and not a free-for-all either: your ordinary attacks, bleeds, only target your prey, on your left, while your predator, on your right, is coming for you. Votes, some cards and a few actions can reach the rest of the table. A turn is actions, blocks, combats and referendums where alliances are made and broken out loud.
rule_1: Awaken your vampires. Each turn you move blood from your pool to your crypt to bring new vampires to the table.
rule_2: Bleed your prey. Your vampires act: a bleed costs your prey blood, unless one of their vampires blocks it and starts a combat.
rule_3: Make the table vote. Titled vampires call referendums that the whole table decides. That is where the most devious plays happen.
what_p3: In Master of the Night, the engine enforces the rules, cards included. When a card gives you a choice, the game offers it to you; when it does not, the game decides and writes it in the game log. You focus on what you want to do; the table knows what is allowed.
shots_lede: Screenshots and clips taken during a game (some with the French interface).
shot_table: The five-player table: your vampires at the bottom, the four other Methuselahs at the top, your prey and your predator marked.
shot_bleed: Your predator bleeds you: the game asks whether you block, and with whom.
shot_council: The Council: drag your votes to For or Against, then confirm.
shot_combat: Combat: choose your strike, with a weapon or bare hands.
shot_resolution: After each action, the game writes down what happened and why, with the maths.
shot_deck: The deck workshop: crypt, library, statistics and the details of every card.
ways_lede: Nobody is born knowing VTES. The game is designed so you can learn it alone in an evening and sit at a real table the next day.
way1_p: Dozens of short lessons played on the real table, not on a mock board: your side of the table, the phases, your first bleed, your first block, a full combat, torpor, allies, votes, paths, sects. Narrated aloud in English and French, written in six languages.
way2_p: AI opponents that play their own deck, block when it matters and know how to get out of torpor. Twenty-one official preconstructed decks, Fifth Edition and New Blood, are included for them and for you.
way3_p: An online table for one to five players, each from their browser or PC. Only three of you? Add two AI opponents to fill the table, or play as three.
way4_p: A deck builder to assemble crypt and library from scratch, or to import an existing deck: a VTES Decks or VDB link, or a pasted list in the usual formats. With an account, your decks follow you from one launch to the next.
plat_lede: Same game, same table. The web version is made for trying and playing without installing anything; the Windows version for those who play often.
plat_r1_web: None. Open the address and play.
plat_r1_win: Download the archive on itch.io, unzip it, launch the game.
plat_r2_web: Always the latest version, nothing to do.
plat_r2_win: The game tells you in the menu when a new version is out.
plat_r3_web: PC, Mac, tablet. Recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
plat_r4_web: Interface in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Turkish.
phys_lede: Master of the Night is for learning and practising. VTES is at its best with cards in hand, facing other players: that is where the deals, the bluffs and the betrayals are real.
phys_shop_p: Starter decks, preconstructed decks and expansions are published by Black Chantry Productions. Their online shop sells directly; their list of distributors and retailers tells you where to find them near you.
phys_tourn_p: The VEKN, the players' association, keeps the calendar of tournaments worldwide, from the local store event to the national championship. A first tournament is the best way to meet the players in your area.
faq1_q: Do I need to know VTES already?
faq1_a: No. The tutorial starts from zero: it shows you your side of the table, then has you play a real turn, a real combat, a real vote, explaining at each step what is happening and why. Allow one evening to feel at home.
faq2_a: Yes. AI opponents fill the five-player table and play their own deck, taken from the official preconstructed decks or from the ones you give them. It is also the best way to test a deck before taking it against humans.
faq3_q: How do I play with my friends?
faq3_a: Create an online table from the game and have your friends join it, from two to five players. The remaining seats can be given to AI opponents, or left empty for a shorter table.
faq4_a: Not to play: open the page and you are at the table, tutorial and games included. An optional account keeps your decks from one launch to the next, and will carry what comes next, such as statistics on your games. It only asks for an email address, a nickname and a password.
faq5_q: Why is the first load long?
faq5_a: The game ships the text and images of every card. Your browser keeps them cached after the first launch, and the next ones are much faster.
faq6_q: Does it work on a phone?
faq6_a: The game runs on a recent phone, but a five-player table with its cards needs room: a PC or tablet screen is far more comfortable.
faq7_a: The game is published in one place only, the itch.io page: if you downloaded it there, you have the right file. The warning comes from Windows, which shows it for any program that has not bought a code-signing certificate — which this free game has not. Click More info, then Run anyway.
faq8_q: Is this the same game as VTES Mobile?
faq8_a: Yes. VTES Mobile is becoming Master of the Night; same table, same engine, same team. The itch.io page keeps its old address so your links keep working.
faq9_a: No. Master of the Night is a fan project, free and without in-app purchases, published under Paradox Interactive's Dark Pack programme. The card game Vampire: The Eternal Struggle is published by Black Chantry Productions, and that is where you buy the real cards.

privacy.title: Privacy and contact
privacy.intro: Master of the Night is a free fan game, with no ads and no in-app purchases. It collects only what it needs to work. This page says what, why, where, and how to have it erased.
s: You can open the game, follow the tutorial and play games without providing anything. The site and the game set no tracking cookies: the site's only cookie remembers your language ("lang", one year).

If you create an account, we store an email address, a nickname and a password. The password is never stored in clear text: it is hashed by the authentication service. The account keeps your decks from one launch to the next and will carry upcoming features, such as statistics on your games.

Accounts and decks are stored with Supabase, a database hosting provider, on the infrastructure it runs for us. The site and the game are served by Cloudflare, which keeps technical logs (IP address, pages requested) for security and load measurement. We do not sell, rent or share any data.
When you report a problem from the game, the text you type and the state of the game in question are sent so that we can reproduce the fault. They are used for nothing else.

At the end of each game, the game sends an anonymous summary: the game version, the number of players, whether the game was online, whether it was played to the end, the number of turns, the list of cards that were used (with how many times) and the choices the interface had to show as a list. This summary contains no account, no username, no address and no device identifier: nothing links it to you. It is used to find cards that have never been played, to confirm those that work, and to improve the interface.

To know how many people play, the game sends a sign of life at most once a day, when it starts: a randomly generated installation identifier kept on your device, the date, the game version and the platform (web, Windows, Android…). This identifier says nothing about you or your device and is not linked to any account: it is only used to count each installation once per day. These records are deleted after 400 days. To start over with a new identifier, simply clear the game's (or the site's) data on your device.
The itch.io page and the Discord server are run by those services, under their own rules. We only see what you post there.
Write to us from the account's email address: it is deleted, decks included, within fifteen days. You can also ask for a copy of what we hold about you.
privacy.contact_p: For any question, deletion request or problem: contact@masterofthenight.com. To talk about the game, the Discord.
